2026 subsidy cliff for a household of 4 in FL: income up to $128,600.00 (400% FPL) gets $11,191.44 a year toward a $24,000.00 benchmark plan; $1 more gets $0.00. Cliff loss: $11,191.44. At $130,000.00 (404.35% FPL) the 2026 credit is $0.00; under the expired enhanced rules it would be $12,950.00. Cutting modified AGI by $1,400.00 would restore $11,191.44.

General information, not tax advice. The Marketplace and Form 8962 decide the official amounts. Benchmark (second lowest cost silver) premiums vary by ZIP code, age and household; get yours from HealthCare.gov or your state Marketplace.

structuredContent.explanation: For 2026 coverage, household income of $128,600 (400% of the 2025 poverty line for 4) still gets a credit; $1 more gets none. The enhanced 2021-2025 rules had no cliff: above 400% the benchmark plan cost was capped at 8.5% of income.
structuredContent.law_status: Enhanced premium tax credits (American Rescue Plan Act and Inflation Reduction Act) applied to tax years 2021 through 2025 only. IRS PTC Q&A (Q7, updated Feb. 19, 2026) says the 400% FPL limit was lifted for 2021 through 2025. No public law of the 119th Congress through P.L. 119-136 (Oct. 22, 2026) amends IRC sec. 36B to extend them (checked: Consolidated Appropriations Act 2026, Continuing Appropriations and Extensions Act 2027 and the other appropriations acts contain no sec. 36B text). For 2026 coverage the 400% FPL limit applies and Rev. Proc. 2025-25 sets the table (2.10% to 9.96%). Checked 2026-11-02; if Congress acts later, this server is out of date.
